walkthroughs.body_html:
Numerical Methods — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Numerical Methods brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Numerical Methods.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

The trapezium rule estimates which kind of quantity?
options: a definite integral
a derivative
a sum to infinity
a stationary point
7 - x — the minus sign outside the bracket changes the sign of every term inside (3 - x + 4).
3x - 12, by multiplying 3 by everything inside.
Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
3 - x - 4 = -1 - x, by only applying the minus to the first term inside.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
3x - 12, by multiplying 3 by everything inside.
The square root of x (the positive root when x is positive).
x^(1/2) means x divided by 2 — half of x.
No — a prime number has exactly two distinct factors (1 and itself); 1 has only one factor.
Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
Yes — 1 has no factors except itself, which makes it prime.
